title: Credibility Lifecycle Pocket Playbook — Alpha
body:
Purpose
---
This is a slim, operational playbook for SEs and sellers to quickly build credibility across the pilot lifecycle: qualify -> pilot -> scale. The goal is not to replace our larger decks but to give rapid, repeatable lines, demo hooks, and evidence snippets that win skeptical platform and security stakeholders.

How to use this doc
- 1-page quick reference to print or stash in notes.
- Use the demo hooks during live walk-throughs. Keep to 30–90s micro-assertions.
- Swap evidence cards depending on persona (platform engineer, security, product).

Quick thesis: People buy on trust + measurable risk reduction. We short-circuit buying friction by pairing one credibility move + one operational proof for every objection.

Persona playlets (30–45s lines)
- Platform engineer: "We treat your SLOs like our product metric. During pilot we recommend a reserved pool with canary routing; that lets you baseline latency and then expand traffic gradually. We’ll provide token-level traces and an SLA experiment plan so you can validate tail latency without guessing."
- Security/compliance: "We can run a private control plane in your VPC or an on-prem package. We'll do a short architecture review and deliver a documented key management checklist and audit event example within the first week."
- Product owner/PM: "We focus on 3 KPIs for pilot: latency, per-call cost, and correctness on 10 golden prompts. If we hit targets after two weeks, we move to a scale runbook — otherwise we joint-debug and iterate prompts/configs."

Demo hooks (for 5–10 minute walkthroughs)
- Hook A (latency-first): Show live inference for a 256-token prompt on two model variants (fast quantized vs. higher-quality): time the responses, then flip to our console trace showing prefix cache hit and batching snapshot. Say: "Here’s where batching saved 40% cost without affecting tail latency for short prompts."
- Hook B (fallback story): Trigger a synthetic overload and demonstrate automated fallback to a cheaper model with preserved schema output. Evidence: console audit log + user-visible response that degrades gracefully.
- Hook C (security): Walk through the VPC topology diagram and show an HSM key rotation event from audit logs; highlight retention policy. Keep diagram to 3 boxes.

Evidence snippets (pasteable)
- "Customer X reduced per-token spend 28% by enabling prefix caching + low-latency batching (pilot, 6 weeks)."
- "Platform Y validated 99.95% availability over a 30-day dedicated pool run at 75% baseline load."
- Metric snapshot: "median latency: 85ms; P99: 230ms; tokens/sec: 230k on a 4-GPU pool (note: config=quant-8+kv-cache)."

Objection response matrix (one-liners)
- "We can’t depend on a hosted API for PHI": "We’ll offer Private deployment with customer-managed control plane and KMS integration; proof-of-work in <14 days."
- "Costs are unpredictable": "We provide a reserved capacity plan and a forecasting workbook; start with a 30% commit to lock unit economics while you ramp."
- "Model quality drifts": "We ship a small eval harness that runs golden prompts on every rollout and alerts on quality regressions; you own the acceptance gate."

Slide-outline for a short credibility deck (6 slides)
- 1: Title + single-line thesis (latency, cost, reliability).
- 2: Risk map for the buyer (top 3 risks + one-sentence mitigation each).
- 3: Quick architecture (3-box VPC/private/hosted).
- 4: Live demo plan + measurable success criteria.
- 5: Case evidence (2 short bullets + metric).
- 6: Next steps + pilot checklist.

Pilot checklist (week 0–2)
- Kickoff: stakeholders, KPIs, success criteria, SSO/KMS contacts.
- Infra: network whiteboard, IP allowlist, resource sizing.
- Data & prompts: 10 golden prompts + 50 representative samples.
- Observability: configure traces, token-level cost, fallback policy test.
- First-run: run 10k inference calls with tracing ON; collect P50/P95/P99.

Practice notes for SEs
- Keep demo hooks tight; rehearse two handoffs: one for platform, one for security.
- Have 3 evidence cards ready and pick the most relevant. Don’t show more than one architecture slide.
- If a live demo hiccups, pivot quickly to recorded trace + postmortem plan; call out resilience story.

Open questions / TODOs
- Collect 4–6 anonymized pilot metrics we can reuse as templates (ask CS for permission).
- Canonicalize the one-page architecture diagram (ask design for a simplified SVG).
- Add a short scripted fallback simulation (SRE + demo script).

Notes to self
- This is alpha: expect to prune redundant evidence and shorten hooks. Share with SEs for feedback at Monday sync.
- Cross-link: pilot-runbook-draft and reserved-capacity-negotiation-playbook.
